diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any bounded function $v : [0,1] \times \mathbb{R}^{3d} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the time and spatial H\"older-Lipschitz condition:

issues.failure_explanation: The integral defining $v^{\varepsilon}$ uses $v(t-\tau)$ with $\tau\in[-\varepsilon^2,0]$, so $t-\tau=t+|\tau|\ge t$. When $t$ is close to $1$, $t-\tau$ exceeds $1$, outside the stated domain $[0,1]$ of $v$. Thus $v^{\varepsilon}$ is not well-defined on all of $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}^{3d}$ as written. This also affects the subsequent claim that $u^{\varepsilon}$ is a supersolution near $t=1$, since the required values of $u$ at future times are unavailable.

failure_location.quote: v^{\varepsilon}(t,x,y,z) := (v \ast \zeta_{\varepsilon})(t,x,y,z) := \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e) \, de \, d\tau,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the mollifier to integrate over past times, e.g. use $v(t+\tau)$ with $\tau\in[-\varepsilon^2,0]$ or equivalently integrate $v(t-\tau)$ with $\tau\in[0,\varepsilon^2]$, and verify that past-time mollification preserves the required viscosity supersolution property; alternatively, extend $v$ beyond $[0,1]$ and prove the extension has the needed property.
issues.overall_effect: The regularization construction and the supersolution property of $u^{\varepsilon}$ and $u_h^{\varepsilon}$ are unsupported near the terminal time, undermining the proofs of the main error bounds.
issues.title: Mollifier uses future time values outside the time domain
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and standard for mollification, but it requires a small additional argument to preserve the supersolution property and to define the mollified functions on the whole time interval.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\partial_t \omega(t - \tau h, x + h^{\frac{1}{2}} X, y, z) - \partial_t \omega(t - \tau h, x, y, z) \\
&= \langle \partial_t D_x \omega(t - \tau h, x, y, z), h^{\frac{1}{2}} X \rangle \\
& \quad + \int_0^1 \int_0^1 \langle \partial_t D_x^2 \omega(t - \tau h, x + v u h^{\frac{1}{2}} X, y, z) h^{\frac{1}{2}} X, h^{\frac{1}{2}} X \rangle u \, du \, dv.

issues.failure_explanation: After bounding $R_{12}$ by an integral of absolute values, the $x$-shift term is $\hat{\mathbb{E}}[|L+R|]$ with $L=h^{1/2}\langle \partial_t D_x\omega,X\rangle$. The linear term $L$ does not cancel inside the absolute value, so this term is generally of order $h^{1/2}$, not $h$. The displayed conclusion omits this $h^{1/2}$ contribution. The correct argument should keep the signed difference and use $\hat{\mathbb{E}}[-L-R]\le \hat{\mathbb{E}}[-L]+\hat{\mathbb{E}}[-R]=\hat{\mathbb{E}}[-R]$ (or the analogous bound) to cancel the zero-mean linear term.

failure_location.quote:
R_{12} \leq {} & \int_0^1 \hat{\mathbb{E}} \big[ \big| \partial_t \omega(t - \tau h, x + h^{\frac{1}{2}} X, y, z) - \partial_t \omega(t - \tau h, x, y, z) \big| \big] \, d\tau \\
\leq {} & \|\partial_t D_z \omega\|_\infty M_Z h^{\frac{1}{\alpha}} + \Big( \|\partial_t D_y \omega\|_\infty M_{Y_1}^1 + \frac{1}{2} \|\partial_t D_x^2 \omega\|_\infty M_{X_1}^2 \Big) h,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the unnecessary absolute value for the $x$-shift part of $R_{12}$ and bound the signed difference directly using subadditivity and the zero-mean condition on $X$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma consistency as written contains an invalid inference. Although the final bound may still be true, the current argument does not establish it, so all downstream error bounds that rely on this lemma are not rigorously proved.
issues.title: Invalid dropping of a linear term inside an absolute value in the time-consistency estimate
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local change to the proof, does not alter the lemma's statement, and does not require new global arguments or reoptimization.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed interpolation uses $q_1=3/2$ and exponent $q_1-\delta$. It is valid only when $q_1\ge\delta$, i.e. $\delta\le 3/2$. Assumption (v) allows $\delta$ up to $\alpha$, which can exceed $3/2$ when $\alpha>3/2$. For such $\delta$, the exponent $3/2-\delta$ is negative, so the inequality is false. In fact, the actual $R_{21}$ term has a leading contribution of order $h^{1/\alpha-1/2}$ from small $|Z|$, which is larger than the claimed $h^{2\delta/(3\alpha)-1/2}$ when $\delta>3/2$. Thus Lemma consistency is not valid for the full parameter range allowed by Assumption (v).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict $\delta$ to $\delta\le 3/2$ in Assumption (v), or replace the invalid interpolation by a correct bound for $\delta>3/2$ (e.g. use a different Hölder exponent or a truncation argument), and reoptimize the rate; the final rate may need to be weakened if the stronger $\delta$-dependent estimate is lost.
issues.overall_effect: For $\alpha>3/2$ and $\delta>3/2$, the consistency estimate and the resulting error bounds $E_1,E_2$ are not established. The convergence-rate proofs depending on Lemma consistency are invalid in that regime.
issues.title: Interpolation in R21 requires δ ≤ 3/2 but Assumption (v) allows δ > 3/2
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false for a parameter range explicitly allowed by the assumptions, and the main convergence-rate results rely on it. A repair requires a nontrivial modification of the consistency proof and possibly of the final rate, not just a local typo correction.
